text:
mina: quick idea — what if we add a short-lived RBAC lease that executors can request so heavy tenants avoid repeated policy lookups? pairs nicely with adaptive batching

raf: curious — lease semantics? owned by executor? renewable?

mina: executor requests a lease for tenant T for N seconds. while lease active, the access-shim serves policies from a pinned entry (local fast path). lease is renewable but revocable by policy-store events (webhook)

jordan: main risk is staleness on policy updates and extra state management. how do we invalidate quickly?

mina: proposal: when policy-store accepts an update it publishes an invalidation to control-plane which fans out a small revocation message to executors. revocation path should be optimized for size and fanout; we also keep a TTL safety so leases expire automatically

yun: this could help batching too — leased tenants allow larger batch sizes since RBAC is local. but we must limit concurrent leases to avoid memory blowup

mina: rough config I sketched:
```
console.rbac_lease = {
  default_ttl_sec: 45,
  max_ttl_sec: 90,
  max_concurrent_leases_region: 500,
  executor_lease_limit: 20,
  lease_expiry_jitter_ms: 5000,
  pinned_cache_size_per_executor: 1024
}
console.adaptive_batching = {
  headway_ms_default: 3,
  headway_ms_max: 30,
  rps_threshold_for_scale: 60,
  base_max_batch: 40,
  leased_max_batch: 160,
  queue_depth_limit: 300
}
```

raf: safety valves: limit leases per executor, queue depth caps (fail-fast), and a shedding policy for overloaded executors. also define behaviour on lease-revoke race: requests in-flight that used stale policy should be logged and optionally soft-blocked for max 25ms to recheck

jordan: telemetry needed: lease_acquire, lease_release, lease_revoked, lease_expired, lease_miss_rate, batch_size_histogram_by_tenant, queue_depth_gauge. alerts: lease_revocations_percentile_latency > 200ms, lease_acquire_fail_rate > 0.5%

yun: rollout thought: simulate in harness first (mixed-tenant + token rotation storms). then canary leases disabled to validate batching improvements. enable leases for 0.5% tenants behind FF console.rbac_lease.v1 and monitor revocation latency and p99 tail

mina: also propose an emergency mode: admin toggle that disables all leases and forces shim to remote-check every request (fail-safe). plus an allow-stale header for non-critical dashboards (x-console-allow-stale-lease)

raf: owners? I can implement the executor portion with mina. jordan helps revocation channel. yun owns telemetry + alerts. infra to create FF

infra-bot: deploybot: feature-flag console.rbac_lease.v1 created by mina. use /deploy-canary to start canary

yun: I'll draft the runbook: initial canary checks (lease_miss_rate, revocation_latency_p95, p99 request latency delta), and rollback criteria (revocation_latency_p95 > 500ms or p99 latency up > 7%)

mina: final note — include a token-rotation test in evals and a policy-update storm scenario. want to make sure revocation fanout doesn't take out control-plane. I'll add a doc link when I open the PR

raf: :thumbsup: schedule 30m sync after PR is ready

mina: thanks all
